deck: This week, investment in space continues, while sensors and strategic partnerships gain traction.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190 million Series C round, boosting its valuation to $1.6 billion. This funding is particularly notable as the company focuses on co-orbital security and space domain awareness, areas increasingly prioritized by the DoD. With defense budgets tightening, this kind of cash infusion suggests a strong belief in the need for enhanced space security measures.
stories.soWhat: Investors clearly see the writing on the wall: as space becomes a contested domain, the demand for security solutions is only going to grow.

stories.head: Look Up and Skynopy team up for collision avoidance
stories.body: Look Up and Skynopy announced a partnership to develop an automated satellite collision avoidance service. This comes at a time when the number of active satellites is skyrocketing, and the risk of collision is becoming a pressing concern. The financial terms weren't disclosed, but the collaboration signals a growing recognition of the importance of space traffic management.
stories.soWhat: If this service works, we might finally have a way to keep our satellites from playing bumper cars in orbit.

stories.head: $1.4B added for space resilience in FY27 budget
stories.body: The FY27 budget markup has allocated an additional $1.4 billion for space resilience, reflecting a shift in how the U.S. government views its space assets. This funding aims to bolster capabilities against potential threats, which have been increasingly highlighted by recent geopolitical tensions. The budgetary increase is a clear signal that space is no longer an afterthought.
stories.soWhat: It's about time space got the budgetary love it deserves; let's hope it translates into actual capabilities and not just more PowerPoint slides.

watchlist.title: Watch for Dawn Aerospace's next steps
watchlist.body: With a recent $25 million raise, Dawn Aerospace is poised to scale its in-space transportation efforts, potentially shaking up suborbital access.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on Sierra Space's Dream Chaser
watchlist.body: Having passed a critical design review, the Dream Chaser's next phase could be pivotal for its future in government contracts.

watchlist.title: Anduril and L3Harris's SDA bid outcome
watchlist.body: Their collaboration on a tactical SDA constellation could redefine how the military approaches space operations; results are expected soon.

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's market impact post-funding
watchlist.body: With significant new capital, True Anomaly's moves in the co-orbital security space could influence competitors and investor sentiment.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
